projects.name: GUI Murphy
projects.summary: AI-driven automated QA system for modern applications, focused on GUI behavior beyond pixel diffs.
details: Understands UI state transitions and validates multi-step user journeys via vision + language reasoning
Pipeline mentions OmniParser (YOLOv8), CLIP, and LLM reasoning
Real-time progress streaming (FastAPI + WebSockets) conceptually fits a live demo

caseStudy.problem: Traditional QA automation tools rely on pixel-perfect comparisons or brittle selectors that break with minor UI changes. Modern apps with dynamic content need semantic understanding of what the UI is doing, not just how it looks.
caseStudy.approach: Built a vision-language pipeline combining OmniParser (YOLOv8) for UI element detection, CLIP for semantic matching, and LLM reasoning to understand user journeys. The system validates behavioral correctness rather than visual similarity.
challenges: Achieving real-time inference speed while maintaining accuracy across diverse UI frameworks
Handling dynamic content and async state changes in SPAs
Building a robust test specification language that non-technical QA could use

async def validate_journey(screens: List[Screenshot]):

    semantics = clip.encode(elements)
    return llm.reason(semantics, expected_behavior)

projects.name: QuantFlow
projects.summary: AI-driven crypto trading engine combining regime detection and probabilistic forecasting for systematic strategy execution.
details: 3-state Hidden Markov Model for bull/bear/sideways regime detection
LightGBM quantile regression (q10/q50/q90) with triple-barrier labeling
Walk-forward backtesting engine with realistic slippage and fee simulation

caseStudy.problem: Most retail algo-trading systems either ignore market regimes entirely or rely on simplistic moving-average crossovers. The result: strategies that work well in trending markets blow up during high-volatility or mean-reverting periods.
caseStudy.approach: Built a two-layer ML stack: a 3-state HMM labels each bar as bull/bear/sideways and gates which signals are allowed to fire; per-regime LightGBM models then produce probabilistic forecasts (q10/q50/q90) using triple-barrier labels. A walk-forward backtesting harness validates out-of-sample before any live capital is risked.
challenges: Avoiding lookahead bias in walk-forward splits with time-series aware cross-validation
Calibrating triple-barrier labels so the regime detector and signal model train on consistent targets
Serving low-latency predictions from TimescaleDB continuous aggregates without blocking the order loop
metrics: Sharpe ratio 1.2 (post-fee 0.8) on out-of-sample test period
Max drawdown -11.3% vs -31% for buy-and-hold benchmark
HMM regime classifier 78% accuracy on held-out data

projects.name: LifeOps
projects.summary: Personal operations bot that consolidates Gmail, Outlook, and Canvas into a unified digest with AI triage and a Telegram interface.
details: Delta polling via Gmail History API and Outlook delta-link — no full mailbox scans
Dual-LLM pipeline: Gemini Flash Lite for triage scoring, Claude for structured extraction
Priority Velocity Index (PVI) engine surfaces high-signal items before they become urgent

caseStudy.problem: Important messages across email, academic portals, and calendars get lost in noise. Manually triaging three inboxes daily is repetitive work that a well-designed system should handle.
caseStudy.approach: Built an incremental sync layer using Gmail's History API and Outlook's delta-link to fetch only changed messages — avoiding full mailbox scans. A dual-LLM pipeline runs Gemini Flash Lite for cheap triage scoring, then routes high-signal items to Claude for structured extraction (deadlines, action items, entities). A Telegram bot delivers the final digest and supports natural-language queries against the stored context.
challenges: Keeping delta tokens valid across restarts and handling full resync gracefully when they expire
Designing the PVI engine to surface urgency without generating alert fatigue
Coordinating two LLM providers with different rate limits inside a single async pipeline
metrics: 95% reduction in API calls vs naive polling approach
~92% extraction accuracy on deadline and action-item detection
caseStudy.codeHighlight:
# Dual-LLM triage pipeline
async def process_message(msg: RawMessage) -> DigestItem | None:
    score = await gemini_flash.triage(msg.snippet)   # cheap gate
    if score < TRIAGE_THRESHOLD:
        return None
    item = await claude.extract(msg.full_body,         # deep parse
        schema=DigestItem)
    item.pvi = pvi_engine.score(item)                  # urgency ranking
    return item

projects.name: Agentformer
projects.context: AIT x Redis x Cloudflare Mini-Hack
projects.summary: AI agent orchestration system enabling multi-agent collaboration for complex task completion.
details: Multi-agent coordination with Redis pub/sub for real-time communication
Cloudflare Workers for edge-deployed agent execution

caseStudy.problem: Single-agent AI systems hit capability ceilings on complex tasks. Multi-agent systems exist but suffer from coordination overhead, message passing bottlenecks, and difficulty in maintaining shared state.
caseStudy.approach: Built a distributed agent orchestration layer using Redis pub/sub for real-time coordination, Cloudflare Workers for edge execution, and a central state manager on GCP. Agents can spawn, communicate, and delegate seamlessly.
challenges: Minimizing coordination latency across distributed agents
Handling agent failures gracefully with task reassignment
Preventing infinite loops in agent-to-agent delegation
